Beyond Earth Labs combines seven NASA challenges into one planetary exploration platform. Using NASA data and deep learning, it connects Earth, Mars, and the Moon through autonomous rovers, terrain analysis, astronaut safety, mission simulations, sustainable farming, and continuous learning.

details:
Beyond Earth Labs — Project Details

Beyond Earth Labs is an AI-powered, three-dimensional planetary exploration and mission-planning platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. I selected NASA's Martian Map challenge as the primary objective and used six additional challenge themes as supporting building blocks: Earth analog discovery, rover navigation, astronaut safety, mission simulation and training, lunar mapping, and space agriculture.

What Does the Project Do?

The platform integrates 20 NASA datasets from five missions into a unified 3D environment centered on Jezero Crater, Mars. It combines satellite imagery, elevation models, thermal observations, and rover imagery to support planetary terrain analysis and mission planning.

The core mission-planning system operates through three stages: Plan, Check, and Run.

During planning, the platform calculates potential routes using NASA elevation data and terrain constraints. It then evaluates oxygen and battery requirements, including reserves necessary for the return journey. During simulated mission execution, unexpected events such as dust storms, obstacles, equipment failures, or astronaut emergencies can trigger route reassessment and contingency planning.

Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning

I incorporated a Vision Transformer-based deep learning model to analyze terrain from Earth, Mars, and the Moon. The model learns visual characteristics of planetary landscapes and identifies Earth locations that resemble Martian terrain.

This capability could help researchers identify suitable environments for testing robotic equipment and rehearsing planetary missions before deployment.

The AI component is intentionally separated from safety-related navigation calculations. Machine learning supports research and terrain discovery, while route planning relies on geographic data and defined traversal constraints.

Space Agriculture and Sustainable Habitation

The agriculture component explores the resource requirements of greenhouse operations on Mars. It considers the water, electricity, nutrients, lighting, and environmental controls required to support plant cultivation in a protected habitat.

By incorporating greenhouse resource demands into the broader mission-planning framework, the platform demonstrates how exploration activities and long-term habitation could be evaluated together.

Technologies and Development

The project combines NASA planetary datasets, geospatial processing, 3D visualization, terrain-aware routing algorithms, resource-feasibility modeling, and deep learning.

Scientific information is drawn from NASA planetary archives, including observations associated with the Mars 2020 Perseverance mission. The artificial intelligence component uses Vision Transformer techniques for planetary terrain representation and similarity analysis.

Automated software testing was also incorporated to evaluate the functionality of the prototype. The project reports 73 passing automated tests and a median terrain elevation difference of approximately one meter compared with selected Perseverance reference measurements.

The platform operates as a software research prototype, with rover operations, astronaut emergencies, and greenhouse resource requirements represented through computational models and simulations rather than physical hardware.

Innovation and Intended Impact

The project's primary innovation is its integrated architecture. Rather than developing seven unrelated solutions, I used six supporting NASA challenge themes to expand the Martian Map into a comprehensive exploration-planning environment.

This approach connects navigation, astronaut safety, environmental analysis, artificial intelligence, mission simulation, and sustainable habitation within a single platform.

Throughout development, I considered scientific data accuracy, terrain uncertainty, computational reliability, resource limitations, environmental hazards, AI generalization, and the distinction between simulated conditions and real mission measurements.

The long-term goal of Beyond Earth Labs is to demonstrate how scientific data and intelligent software can work together to make planetary exploration safer, more efficient, and more sustainable.

Formal Technical Report: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NKqcbI3NfwnjVq-Ea7o-_y9rE1zDmm7e0RjbcGeaFpk/edit
